title: Rabbi Abba bar Shumani
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Eruvin 64a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.64a.10), he and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeyah of Gifti or Difti take leave of each other at the river-crossing of Bana Yofti. They say: “Let each of us state a teaching the other has not heard, for Mari bar Rav Huna said,” etc.[^1]

Hyman has already explained in the entry on Rav Menashia bar Yirmeya that he lived approximately in the time of Rav Ashi, contrary to Mishpachot Sofrim, which has Rabbi Abba bar Shumani in the second generation. In Dikdukei Soferim he cites various readings: Rabbah Shimi or Shimni; and in Yuchasin HaShalem he reads Rava bar Shumani.[^2]

notes.text: The Bavli names Rabbi Abba bar Shumni and Rav Menashya bar Yirmeyah of Gifti. They part at the crossing of the Yofti River. Both propose sharing a teaching the other has not heard.

Heilprin discusses the variants under [Menashya bar Yirmeyah](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2523&lang=en) and [Rabbah bar Shumni](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3175&lang=en). His entries distinguish the wording in the Gemara from readings he assigns to Ein Yaakov and Yuchasin. Hyman’s dating and his other reported names are retained.
